title: Content sustainability guidelines
description: This list of good practices is extracted from the practical guide originally published by Ferréole Lespinasse / Cyclop Éditorial at Publishroom under the title “Sobriété éditoriale, le guide pour écoconcevoir vos contenus“ in Mai 2025.

criteres.bestpractice: The home page addresses the most common audience intentions.
criteres.goals:
- 	Save users time by providing answers to their questions. 
- Facilitate the user's path through the site.
- Initiate user paths that start right from the home page.
criteres.rules: The home page highlights and gives direct access to the most frequently visited information on the site.

criteres.bestpractice: Navigation menus are clear and easy to understand.
criteres.goals:
- Provide easy access to content.
- Guide the user by facilitating navigation through the sections.
criteres.rules: The site menu uses meaningful, concise and precise words.

criteres.bestpractice: The footer is useful to the user and complements the menu.
criteres.goals:
- Support navigation.
- Provide users with useful and necessary information, wherever they may be in the site.
criteres.rules: The footer does not repeat the menu, and includes the essentials: legal notice, accessibility statement (if required by law), environmental statement, and data privacy policy.

criteres.bestpractice: A breadcrumb guides the visitor through the site.
criteres.goals:
- Facilitate navigation and inform users where they are.
- Facilitate access to upper-level pages.
- Indicate where the current page is located in the site architecture.
- Optimize site referencing.
criteres.rules: A breadcrumb trail reflects the navigation menu.

criteres.bestpractice: Navigation pages introduce and summarize lower level pages.
criteres.goals:
- Facilitate navigation between pages.
- Provide an overall view of available content to help the user avoid unnecessary clicks.
- Promote referencing.
criteres.rules: Pages with lower levels contain a table of contents allowing access to these sub-pages.

criteres.bestpractice: Navigation link labels are self-explanatory.
criteres.goals:
- Guide navigation. 
- Simplify the transition to action (call-to-action).
- Reduce uncertainty.
criteres.rules: Navigation links of the same nature are written identically.

criteres.bestpractice: Pages are optimized for SEO.
criteres.goals:
- Make sure the page is properly indexed. 
- Enhance the page's findability to best meet search intent.
criteres.rules: All pages include Title and Meta description tags.

criteres.bestpractice: The Title tag indicates the purpose of the page.
criteres.goals:
- Identify page content.
- Respond to the search intention.
- Attract clicks.
criteres.rules: The Title tag contains the page's main keyword.

criteres.bestpractice: The Meta description tag describes the content of the page.
criteres.goals:
- Identify page content. 
- Respond to the search intention.
- Attract clicks.
criteres.rules: The Meta description tag summarizes the content of the page and encourages the reader to consult it.

criteres.bestpractice: Links in the content are relevant.
criteres.goals:
- Facilitate access to information for the reader.
- Provide a comprehensive overview of a subject. 
- Prioritize access to information.
criteres.rules: The links in the text are relevant to the subject.

criteres.step:
Characterization of the organisation 
and content
criteres.bestpractice: The organization is presented in a unique way.
criteres.goals:
- Bring out what makes the organization unique, what sets it apart from other organizations.
- Limit the possibility of making the organization sound like others.
criteres.rules: Content about the organization is not interchangeable with content from other organizations.

criteres.step:
Characterization of the organisation 
and content
criteres.bestpractice: Organizational commitments can be verified.
criteres.goals:
- 	Ensure trust between the user and the organization.
- Give concrete, tangible form to the organization's commitments, to meet the public's need for transparency.
criteres.rules: Promises, arguments and announcements are backed up by facts: figures, testimonials, social proof, indicators, etc.

criteres.step:
Characterization of the organisation 
and content
criteres.bestpractice: Content and messaging are consistent throughout the organization.
criteres.goals: - Prove the organization's alignment between words and deeds.
criteres.rules: Content is consistent between channels: websites, newsletters, presentation pages on social networks, printed materials.

criteres.step:
Characterization of the organisation 
and content
criteres.bestpractice: The overall messaging of every piece of content is objective.
criteres.goals:
- Avoid cognitive bias. 
- Embody ethical, objective and sincere communication. 
- Reinforce the legitimacy of the organization's statements (public positions).
criteres.rules: Does the information provided in the information piece enable you to construct a concrete, factual and objective representation of the subject?

criteres.step:
Characterization of the organisation 
and content
criteres.bestpractice: The site showcases the organization's achievements.
criteres.goals:
- Illustrate the organization's way of doing things.
- Prove the effectiveness of the method.
- Allow the public to project themselves.
criteres.rules: The site features the organization's achievements, either in a section or on dedicated pages.

criteres.step:
Characterization of the organisation 
and content
criteres.bestpractice: Content is not repetitive.
criteres.goals:
- Avoid duplicate content.
- Prioritize content updates over new page creation.
criteres.rules: Check the sitemap and use internal search to ensure that planned content doesn't already exist on the organization's site.

criteres.step:
Characterization of the organisation 
and content
criteres.bestpractice: All media used in content adds value.
criteres.goals: - Support understanding of content.
criteres.rules: Media cannot be replaced by headers or alternative layouts.

criteres.step:
Characterization of the organisation 
and content
criteres.bestpractice: The objectives of the communication piece are immediately understandable.
criteres.goals: - Make it obvious why the communication piece is valuable.
criteres.rules: As soon as they arrive on the support, users immediately understand what they can expect from it.

criteres.step:
Characterization of the organisation 
and content
criteres.bestpractice: Content is useful for the user.
criteres.goals:
- Avoid informational overload.
- Remove content that doesn't serve the purpose of the page.
- Avoid unnecessary cognitive load.
- Encourage referencing by search engines on specific subjects.
criteres.rules: Content meets the user's information needs: who, what, why, where, when, how, how much?

criteres.bestpractice: The information is easy to find in the overall message.
criteres.goals:
- Enable users to easily absorb content
- Encourage the reader's intellectual path, helping the user move more easily from one stage to the next.
- Make it easier for users to find information on the page, and to access content via multiple paths.
criteres.rules: Formatting is used to provide hierachy in the content.

criteres.bestpractice: All content components on the web page are important to the overall message.
criteres.goals: - Deliver all the content users need right where they are.
criteres.rules: The page interface includes information needed to support the user's comprehension. At the very least, it includes the organization's identity and value proposition.

criteres.bestpractice: The message is easy to understand.
criteres.goals:
- Reduce the user's cognitive load.
- Respect the user's time.
- Avoid uncertainty.
- Reflect the organization's values.
criteres.rules: The message enables users to find what they're looking for, understand what they find and use what they find to meet their needs.

criteres.bestpractice: Information is easy to use.
criteres.goals:
- Satisfy user needs.
- Enable expected behavior.
- Meet your organization's communication objectives.
criteres.rules: Information is designed to encourage next-best actions.

criteres.bestpractice: UX content is designed with care.
criteres.goals:
- Make it clear what needs to be done, and reduce doubt.
- Accompany the user's journey.
- Promote web accessibility.
criteres.rules: UX content is short, informative and explicit.

criteres.bestpractice: Titles and subtitles are clear.
criteres.goals: - 	Give users precise information about the content of the page or article.
criteres.rules: Reading the titles and subtitles is enough to get the gist of the message.

criteres.bestpractice: The intro heading summarizes the content of the page.
criteres.goals:
- Save users time by providing a page summary.
- Tell users what the page content is about.
criteres.rules: An intro heading is included if the text is longer than 300 words.

criteres.bestpractice: The tagline complements the title.
criteres.goals:
- Inform readers and save them time.
- Provide a hook that encourages them  to dive into the content.
- On the web, avoid unnecessary clicks.
criteres.rules: A tagline follows the title.

criteres.bestpractice: Sentences are concise.
criteres.goals:
- Be understood on first reading.
- Help text memorization.
- Encourage action.
criteres.rules:
Longer sentences (20 words or more) are used in no more than 25% of the overall text. 
Use the Gunning Fog, Lexicool and Flesh index calculation tools to verify this rule.

criteres.bestpractice: Sentence structure is clear.
criteres.goals:
- Avoid ambiguity.
- Facilitate comprehension from the very first reading.
- Encourage user engagement.
criteres.rules: Did you understand the text on first reading?

criteres.bestpractice: Sentences are precise.
criteres.goals:
- Be understood on first reading.
- Avoid uncertainty.
- Reduce the reader's cognitive load.
criteres.rules: Can you construct a mental representation with the sentences you've just read?

criteres.bestpractice: Words are clear and unambiguous.
criteres.goals:
- Lighten the cognitive load.
- Avoid uncertainty.
criteres.rules: The words used are appropriate to the topic and purpose.

criteres.bestpractice: The text has rhythm.
criteres.goals:
- Support the reader's concentration and interest.
- Involve them and maintain their attention.
criteres.rules: Sentence structures vary, alternating between long, medium and short sentences; and nominal, affirmative, interrogative, or exclamatory sentences.

criteres.bestpractice: Language is inclusive.
criteres.goals: - 	Ensure communication doesn't exclude anyone.
criteres.rules: Use gender-neutral language is used wherever possible.

criteres.bestpractice: Spelling, grammar and punctuation are correct.
criteres.goals:
- 	Reassure the reader about the legitimacy of the message and its sender.
- Ensure readers are not distracted by issues of form.
- Be exemplary.
criteres.rules: The writing process includes a revision/correction stage, either by a third party or by a verification tool.

criteres.bestpractice: Pages that are similar share the same structure.
criteres.goals:
•	Facilitate content absorption thanks to consistent presentation of information.
•	Facilitate information retrieval.
•	Reduce cognitive load.
criteres.rules: Content types are presented in an identical fashion (all your case studies, product pages, skills pages, etc.).

criteres.bestpractice: Information is to the point.
criteres.goals:
- 	Avoid information overload.
- Remove unnecessary information that detracts from the substance of the message.
criteres.rules: Texts do not contain unnecessary elements.

criteres.bestpractice: Information is formatted in a way that makes it easy to understand.
criteres.goals:
- Make reading more fluid.
- Facilitate the reception of information - visual and textual.
criteres.rules: Content is written using a standard style guide.

criteres.bestpractice: Information is segmented into smaller chunks.
criteres.goals:
- 	Encourage users to read all the content.
- Make it easier to access information and click on hyperlinks.
- Use white space to facilitate reading.
- Support memorization.
criteres.rules: Each paragraph contains a singular idea.

criteres.bestpractice: Page layout promotes information scanning.
criteres.goals:
- Chunk information so that readers can easily find what they're looking for.
- Differentiate between primary and secondary information.
- Facilitate the transition from browsing to page reading.
criteres.rules: The visual layout of the page is based on a style sheet.

criteres.bestpractice: The font is easy to read.
criteres.goals:
- Make reading easier.
- Avoid eyestrain.
criteres.rules: Color contrasts are respected, using the Color Review tool https://color.review.

criteres.bestpractice: Content follows accessibility rules.
criteres.goals:
- Make reading easier for people with disabilities.
- Facilitate reading by screen readers.
criteres.rules: The essential rules of accessibility are respected in the texts: contrast of font colors, important information at the beginning, hierarchy of titles, limitation of emojis.

criteres.bestpractice: The choice of communication channels is consistent with the organization's audiences and objectives.
criteres.goals:
- Select channels used by target audiences.
- Allocate just the energy and time needed to achieve results.
- Support the organization's objectives.
criteres.rules: Channel selection is based on examined audience behaviors and expectations.

criteres.bestpractice: Information is published with oversight.
criteres.goals:
- Bring added value to audiences.
- Limit the publishing of information that doesn't meet their needs.
- Support communication objectives.
criteres.rules: Content is published according to clear guidelines and principles.

criteres.bestpractice: Content is presented in the most lightweight and relevant format for the topic at hand.
criteres.goals:
- Determine the most efficient, easiest and lightest format.
- Facilitate the user experience.
- Limit the environmental footprint of communications.
criteres.rules: The choice of content format is based on usefulness and environmental impact.

criteres.bestpractice: Publishing frequency is appropriate and does not overwhelm readers.
criteres.goals:
- Maintain publication quality over time.
- Keep readers' cognitive load to a minimum.
- Preserve the teams responsible for content production.
- On the print side, reduce the number of copies.
criteres.rules: Publishing frequency in each channel takes into account human and environmental impacts.

criteres.bestpractice: Each content item has a defined lifecycle.
criteres.goals:
- Review and update content over time to guarantee its reliability,
- Optimize workloads by anticipating actions,
- Enhance the value of  editorial assets and fight against digital graveyards.
criteres.rules: A content management dashboard exists and indicates date of creation, publication, update, deletion or archiving.

criteres.bestpractice: Content is up-to-date.
criteres.goals:
- Make online information reliable and establish a bond of trust with the user.
- Maintain control over your content and databases. 
- Promote referencing.
criteres.rules: The date of content update is visible on each piece of content.

criteres.bestpractice: Content effectiveness is regularly evaluated.
criteres.goals:
- Track content performance.
- Ensure that content is of interest to audiences.
- Prioritize content for improvement, based on the number of visits.
- Remove low-audience content.
criteres.rules: Indicators for monitoring content effectiveness are defined.
